title: Hall Sloppy Joe Feed
seoTitle: Hall Sloppy Joe Feed | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sweet-tangy beef sloppy joes with buns and chips for ten
subtitle: Sweet-tangy beef sloppy joes with buns and chips for ten
description: Ground beef browns with onion and bell pepper, then simmers in a sweet-tangy tomato sauce until thick and scoopable. Pile on toasted buns with pickles and chips for a classic hall feed.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef with onion and bell pepper over medium-high heat 12–15 minutes, breaking into crumbles until well browned. Drain excess fat.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.instruction: Stir in ketchup, tomato paste, Worcestershire, vinegar, and brown sugar until combined.

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.instruction: Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, stirring often, until sauce mounds on a spoon and flavors meld.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.instruction: Split buns and toast cut-side down in a dry skillet or under broiler at 400°F until golden, about 3 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Serve the line
steps.instruction: Hold beef warm at 165°F in a hotel pan. Crews build sandwiches with pickles and extra onion if desired. Serve with chips.

proTips: A tablespoon of mustard adds tang without making it taste like mustard.
Smoked paprika pinch makes canned-sauce flavors taste more homemade.
Coleslaw on the sandwich is messy but worth it if you have time.
tonightSpread: Sloppy joes with kettle chips and dill pickles.
Baked beans from a can, doctored with molasses and mustard, for a cookout vibe.
leftovers: Serve over baked potatoes with shredded cheese.
Fold into a casserole with tater tots and cheddar for sloppy joe hot dish.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sloppy joes are cheap, fast, and universally loved—especially by crews who grew up on cafeteria versions. This recipe is thicker and meatier, built for ten hungry firefighters.
mealPrepNotes: Brown beef hard and drain fat or sandwiches get greasy. Sauce should mound on a spoon, not run off the bun. Toast buns so they survive the saucy filling.
